Hi Gaurav,

Thanks — we can support the exact scope you described. Below is the high-level workflow we propose, plus a sample confirmation template. I attached the draft runbook and a sample evidence manifest for your review.

High-level purge workflow (scoped tenant):
1) Intake and ticketing: create a one-off purge job in our playbook system (Jira SEC-4981). This pins the tenant ID, assets to remove, and preservation constraints.
2) Dry-run verification: run a read-only sweep to enumerate objects that match the scope (prompts, outputs, logs). Dry-run produces a manifest file and checksum snapshot.
3) Quiesce write paths: temporarily stop ingestion for the scoped tenant and snapshot active KV caches.
4) Targeted deletion: execute deletion across the following layers in order: ephemeral caches, per-instance KV stores, persistent object storage, and centralized request logs. Each deletion action is recorded to our audit ledger (append-only).
5) KV cache eviction confirmation: validate KV cache ids match the dry-run snapshot.
6) Post-delete verification: run an independent verification step that searches for any residual items via query.
7) Evidence package generation: produce evidence_manifest.csv with timestamps, object counts, checksums, and operator IDs. We sign this package and attach operator logs.
8) Confirmation emails and signed manifest delivery: we send three artifacts: an email to your compliance inbox, a signed CSV manifest, and a storage-level deletion certificate.

Sample confirmation email (we can customize wording):
Subject: Redwood purge confirmation for FinBay tenant FB-8342 — 2028-10-20 22:00 UTC
Body:
Hello FinBay Compliance team,

This message confirms that Redwood executed a scoped purge for tenant FB-8342 on 2028-10-20T22:00:00Z. The purge removed scoped prompt inputs, model outputs, and request/response logs per the scoped ticket SEC-4981. Attached: evidence_manifest_signed.csv and deletion_certificate.pdf.
If you require notarization or additional operator logs, reply to this thread and we will provide them within the agreed SLA.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Trust — Redwood Inference

Attachments sent: purge_runbook_v2.pdf, confirmation_email_templates.txt, evidence_manifest.csv

Operational notes:
- Chain-of-custody: every deletion operation is logged with operator ID and monotonic sequence number. We retain deletion audit entries for 90 days per your constraint.
- Tenant isolation: deletes are executed with tenant-scoped selectors; we run a separate verification job that asserts no other tenant objects share the same tenant tag.
- SLA: evidence manifest delivered within 4 business days after the purge completes unless notarization is requested.

If that looks good I will schedule a technical call with Marissa and Connor to finalize cutover windows and the verification queries.

Evelyn

[Attachment: purge_runbook_v2.pdf (pdf)]

> High-level purge workflow (scoped tenant):
> 2) Dry-run verification: run a read-only sweep to enumerate objects that match the scope (prompts, outputs, logs). Dry-run produces a manifest file and checksum snapshot.

Thanks — adding a few technical specifics so your ops team can vet the approach: 
- Dry-run enumerator will output manifest rows in the format: tenant_id, object_type, object_key, created_at, checksum
- Deletion commands are idempotent DELETE calls against the internal object-store API and followed by a tombstone write to the audit ledger.
- Example verification query (pseudo): SELECT count(*) FROM request_logs WHERE tenant_id='FB-8342' AND created_at >= '2026-10-01' AND created_at <= '2028-10-01';
- Cache eviction: we snapshot the active KV keyset and then issue evict(key) operations. Eviction receipts are collected in receipts.log.

We will include the receipts.log excerpt and the exact verification queries in the runbook PDF that Evelyn attached. Please confirm whether you want the signed manifest notarized or if a signed CSV is sufficient for your internal audit.

Marissa
Principal Systems Engineer — Redwood Inference
